reason: The wording and the locator survive; the ATTRIBUTION FORM does not, and that is what I refute. (1) WORDING, read in place. I downloaded Project Gutenberg 2811 with curl and read the line in its paragraph rather than trusting the verifier's transcript. The title page of that file is LETTERS OF PLINY, By Gaius Plinius Caecilius Secundus, Translated by William Melmoth, Revised by F. C. T. Bosanquet, which is the named translation. The sentence stands at line 2161 inside the account of the Elder Pliny's working day: for every book he read he made extracts out of, indeed it was a maxim of his, that “no book was so bad but some good might be got out of it.” Word for word as proposed, with the card supplying the capital N that the translator's own quotation marks make natural. (2) LOCATOR. I listed every letter heading in the file: the headings run I to XXVII and heading XXVII To BAEBIUS MACER stands at line 2113, forty-eight lines above the sentence, so the 1909 selection's number XXVII is right and the letter is the catalogue of the Elder Pliny's writings, which is Epistulae 3.5 in the standard numbering. Book III, letter 5 is correct. The Latin at 3.5.10 is nullum esse librum tam malum ut non aliqua parte prodesset. (3) shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Pliny the Younger 0 of 3, not banned, and no second Pliny among the four lines under review. (4) MECHANICS. Source line 122 characters, leads with the name, no dash, no straight double quote, quotation ends in a full stop, tag Correspondence is the form of the work. (5) SCOPE. Antiquity, not scripture, publishable, and squarely counsel for the month of Wisdom and Counsel. WHY IT IS STILL REFUTED. This is reported speech, and the brief is explicit about it: a line one character REPORTS of another is the reporter's, and THE NOTE SAYS SO. The note field is empty. Worse, the reported man is himself one of the most famous authors in Latin, and the source line calls him only his uncle. A reader of the card sees the byline Pliny the Younger over a maxim that Pliny the Younger twice marks as not his own (it was a maxim of his, inside quotation marks), and is given no way to learn whose it is. That is the Beauty will save the world row of the misattribution table in miniature: real, correctly located, and credited to the reporter without naming the man reported. Fix by naming the Elder in the source line, which still fits at 138 characters, and by ruling the line CORRECTED with a note along these lines: Pliny the Younger reports the maxim as his uncle Pliny the Elder's, inside quotation marks, in the account of the Elder's working day; the capital N is the card's. Nothing else needs to change.
